stem:
Oditi compares $6.3\times 10^{3}$ and $2.1\times 10^{4}$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Compare only the coefficients $6.3$ and $2.1$ and ignore the powers of $10$.
$2.1\times 10^{4}$ is larger because the exponent $4$ is greater than $3$.
The same comparison ranks every pair of numbers, including those not written with powers of $10$.
Add each coefficient to its exponent ($6.3+3$ versus $2.1+4$) to decide the order.

teacher.key_rationale: When exponents differ, order of magnitude decides first: 10^4 beats 10^3, so 2.1×10^4 is larger. Ignoring exponents, extending the rule beyond scientific form, or adding coefficient to exponent are wrong.
